finding.claim: The unvalidated iconUrl field, stored from the icon parameter of update() (PUT /profile), is used as the target of a server-side HTTP GET in the nightly sync(). This is blind SSRF: the response body is discarded, but the request is still sent to attacker-chosen HTTP(S) hosts.
finding.source: icon parameter of update() at src/Profile.java:11 (per the comment on line 10, supplied via PUT /profile; inferred from comment only, not verified in this repo)
finding.sink: c.send(HttpRequest...uri(URI.create(iconUrl)).GET()...) at src/Profile.java:23-24, run from sync() at line 20

trace.note: Comment: PUT /profile is the entry point for update()
update(String webhook, String icon) receives attacker-controlled icon
Only webhook is validated; icon is not checked
this.iconUrl = icon stores the value unvalidated
Comment: sync() is the nightly job
URI.create(iconUrl) builds the request target; GET issued via c.send

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, IP-range, or allow-list validation on icon. JDK HttpClient restricts schemes to http/https, so file:/gopher: are not reachable. Response body is discarded (no data exfiltration; blind SSRF). Default HttpClient does not follow redirects; if the caller's client is configured with Redirect.NORMAL/ALWAYS, redirects could reach internal addresses (client configuration not in repo, unverified). Severity medium, conditional on update() being reachable from untrusted PUT input.

verdict.guard_found: none: src/Profile.java:16 stores icon unvalidated, and no scheme/host/allow-list check exists before URI.create(iconUrl) at src/Profile.java:23-24. Line 12 validates only webhook.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (src/Profile.java:10-24) and no closing guard exists, but the repo contains only src/Profile.java, so nothing shows that the PUT /profile handler exists or that an unauthenticated or low-privilege user can reach update() at line 11; that reachability rests only on the comment at line 10.
